title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is working with combinatorial maps ('cartes') described by the cartographic group. A map is a set R of 'repères', the flags or triangles of the barycentric subdivision. Three involutions τ0, τ1, τ∞ act on R. In this notation ρ1 = τ0τ∞, and the usual relation is (τ0τ∞)^2 = 1, so the cartographic group is C2 = ⟨τ0, τ1, τ∞ | τi^2 = (τ0τ∞)^2 = 1⟩.

Previous page, two degenerate configurations.
- Fixed points of ρ1 (τ0 r = τ∞ r, relation (10)) correspond to 'flattened' (folded) edges. These are type-1 vertices of the barycentric subdivision that are topological endpoints of the complex K.
- Fixed points of ρ0 (τ1 r = τ∞ r, relation (11)) correspond to univalent (terminal) vertices.

This page, part 1.
- Grothendieck first checks a coincidence. Relation (11) does not force τ1 r = τ∞ r = τ0 r. That triple equality would put us in case (10) as well; with the τi acting without fixed points it is in any case still a set with operators of 𝔖2.
- So a fixed point of ρ1 means the type-1 point of the repère lies on a fold ('pli'). Type-0 points cannot be folds, by definition.
- Conclusion: once 'cartes pliées' (folded maps) are admitted, the categorical equivalences (8) and (1) no longer need the hypothesis that ρ1 (alias σ) acts without fixed points.
- The hypothesis that the τi act freely remains for now. Fixed points of a reflection τi would correspond to boundary. He says this restriction will be easy to remove later ('cf plus bas').

This page, part 2.
- The index 1 plays a special role because of the relation ρ1^2 = 1. To remove the asymmetry he introduces (12): Π03^τ = ⟨τ0, τ1, τ∞ | τi^2 = 1⟩ = Z/2 * Z/2 * Z/2, with no relation (τ0τ∞)^2 = 1. This is the extended (∞,∞,∞) triangle group.
- He also introduces its index-2 subgroup (13): Π03 = ⟨ρ0, ρ1, ρ∞ | ρ∞ρ1ρ0 = 1⟩. This is the free group F2, i.e. π1(P1 − {0,1,∞}).
- The margin defines the parity homomorphism Π03^τ → Z/2, τi ↦ 1, whose kernel is Π03.

Next page. With ρ∞ = τ1τ0, ρ1 = τ0τ∞, ρ0 = τ∞τ1, he gets G2 ≅ Π~03/⟨ρ1^2⟩ and the oriented version G2^0 ≅ Π03/⟨ρ1^2⟩. Π~03 then classifies 'weighted triangular maps': triangulations whose vertices are coloured by {0,1,∞}, each face bijectively. These are hypermaps or dessins presented through their barycentric triangulation, possibly non-orientable.

Purpose: to replace the map-specific cartographic group by the symmetric free group on three involutions. This lets maps with folds or boundary, hypermaps and dessins all be handled as finite sets with an action of Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 (or of F2 in the oriented case).
errors: No mathematical errors. Check: ρ∞ρ1ρ0 = τ1τ0·τ0τ∞·τ∞τ1 = 1, consistent with (13); ρ0 and ρ1 freely generate the even subgroup, of index 2.
The opening argument about (11) not implying the triple coincidence is elliptic and partly illegible; its logical status is only sketched.

ideas.what: Folded maps ('cartes pliées'): allow fixed points of ρ1 = τ0τ∞, interpreted as edges folded onto themselves (free or half-edges ending at a type-1 point), so the equivalence between maps and permutation representations no longer needs ρ1 to be fixed-point free
ideas.modern_name: Maps with free edges / semi-edges; non-free actions of the cartographic group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (1978); Bryant–Singerman (1985, maps on surfaces with boundary); Malgoire–Voisin (1977)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the cartographic group and maps; whether it explicitly discusses folded maps is unsure

ideas.what: Fixed points of the reflections τi correspond to boundary; the plan is to drop the freeness hypothesis on the τi later
ideas.modern_name: Maps or hypermaps on surfaces with boundary via the extended triangle group

ideas.what: Symmetrisation: replace C2 by the free product Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 (extended triangle group of type (∞,∞,∞)), whose index-2 even subgroup is F2 = π1(P1 − {0,1,∞}); C2 and its oriented version are quotients by ⟨ρ1^2⟩
ideas.modern_name: Extended triangle group Δ*(∞,∞,∞), hypermaps, dessins d'enfants
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §§2–3 (cartographic group as a quotient; dessins as finite sets with F2-action)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working-out of standard dessin/map formalism: folded maps, then the free product of three involutions with its index-2 free subgroup. It is essentially what appears in the Esquisse and in the Jones–Singerman / Bryant–Singerman theory. Nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Paragraph opening is probably 'Grâce à l'introduction des cartes pliées, dans les équivalences catégoriques (8), il n'est plus nécessaire d'introduire l'hypothèse que ρ1 opère sans pt fixe', not 'Ainsi : l'introduction...'.
'le point de type 1 doit rejoindre un pli' is uncertain; it may read 'le point du type 1 [du repère] est un pli' (the following parenthesis says type-0 points cannot be [folds] by definition).
The group in (12) carries a tilde/τ decoration (Π~03, matching the next page's \tilde{π}_{03}).
The margin note seems to describe the homomorphism Π03^τ → Z/2 (τi ↦ 1 mod 2) with kernel Π03.
